findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: No CFPM was present at time of inspection. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that a CFPM is present at the facility whenever food is being prepped and handled.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Inspector observed no CFPM present at time of inspection. Educated PIC on CFPM requirements. Ensure a CFPM is present during all hours of operation.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed facility to have no sanitizer available for use. PIC stated that fabuloso was being used for sanitizing surfaces. Educated PIC on proper sanitizing agents. Inspector made a sanitizer bucket of bleach and water with PIC and instructed them on how to use it. Ensure sanitizer is available in facility at all times.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P)

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that no employees had their food-handlers certification at time of inspection. Educated PIC on regulations regarding food-handler certifications. Ensure all staff that handle food acquire a food-handler certificate from an accredited course by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

At the time of this inspection, the PIC could not provide signed reporting agreements for the facility food handlers. Another copy of the SCDPH Reporting Agreement was given and they have two weeks to ensure that all food handler employees have signed one.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

A large tub is observed in front of the hand sink in the back storage area. Education conducted and the tub removed to correct. PIC is aware that the hand sinks cannot have anything in front of them to promote good hand washing practices.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The outlet above the hand sink in the employee bathroom has a gap between it and the wall. Seal the space so that there is no gap present.
